newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes extend gains late with WTI - Sept 5.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes extend gains late with WTI - Sept 5.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices extended gains late Thursday as shrinking imports and lower inventories firmed benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the basis for local crudes.
The U.S. government's Energy Information Administration (EIA) showed crude stocks fell by five million barrels last week, to hit 308 million.

And the pace of imports slowed according to data from the trade group American Petroleum Institute. Imports fell to just 6.73 million barrels last week after keeping an eight million barrel clip in previous weeks.

Differentials for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude stayed flat at $2.05 a barrel under October WTI but traders heard a sale may have been concluded between a major producer and a Northwest refiner. Traders claimed the cargo sold at minus at $2.20.
One refiner said prices could tighten for heavy grades near term and saw Kern River grades rising to parity with postings, after weeks of idling at 50 to 75 cents under.

Values for Wilmington stood at $16.60/16.70 cents a gallon while Wilmington remained $14.50/15.00 a barrel, after rising Wednesday with NYMEX-driven posted prices. Line 63 differentials were unchanged at WTI minus $2.60/2.50 a barrel.
